endpoint.name: Google Gemini answer — text and sources
endpoint.summary: Runs a prompt through the live Google Gemini interface from a chosen country and returns the generated answer with its cited sources and citation pills, optionally as Markdown or HTML.
endpoint.call_template: treg call cloro.ai-search.gemini.scrape --method POST --data '{"prompt":"what is a stock split","country":"US","include":{"markdown":true,"html":true,"rawResponse":true}}'

cost.note: 4 base + the 2-credit sync surcharge. Every include flag on this endpoint is free — only `state` moves the price, by 2. A failed extraction is not charged.

prompt.example: how does a heat pump work

country.note: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. BY, CN and RU are refused.

state.note: US state code for state-level targeting; adds 2 credits

include.note: any of markdown, html, rawResponse. All three are free on this endpoint.

endpoint.capability_description: Scrape a live Gemini answer page for a keyword

samples.reason: Returned answer text and sources cheaply. Source URLs carry #:~:text fragments and repeat, so strip and dedupe them before counting citations.
Category-level answer, few named vendors; confirms absence.
Gemini answer with per-claim sources and domains; sources repeat (17 entries, ~6 unique pages), so dedupe by URL before counting citations.

samples.reason: 40/40 answers with many per-paragraph sources; brand_entities absent so business names need text parsing. Flash-Lite model, treat as one sample.
Gemini answer with sources and snippets; no fan-out queries, and the model was a Flash-Lite variant, so treat it as one sample, not the Gemini app experience.
Answers and sources were good for French local queries, but brand_entities came back empty on every call, so brand detection had to be done by text matching.
